name: Richard Jago
credit: Richard Jago, portrait by an unknown artist, 18th century · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Richard Jago (1715–1781) was an English clergyman and poet, a friend and Oxford contemporary of William Shenstone. He is known for his topographical poem Edge-Hill (1767) and for short lyrics such as "Absence".

The poem here is the one printed under his name in Frederick Locker's Lyra Elegantiarum (London: E. Moxon, 1867), an anthology of vers de société and vers d'occasion by deceased authors; the texts follow that first edition.

poems.title: Absence
poems.author: Richard Jago
poems.collection: Lyra Elegantiarum, ed. Frederick Locker (London: E. Moxon, 1867)
poems.text:
With leaden foot Time creeps along,
While Delia is away.
With her, nor plaintive was the song.
Nor tedious was the day.

Ah! envious power! reverse my doom.
Now double thy career;
Strain every nerve, stretch every plume,
And rest them when she's here.
